question.text: A Category II AIF's Investment Manager decides to switch valuation of a portfolio of unlisted investees from 'Last Round Price' (IPEV method 1) to 'DCF' (IPEV method 5) as the primary method. Under current SEBI guidance, how should this be treated?

answer.text: Treated as material only if NAV impact exceeds 5%
Requires prior SEBI approval before implementation
Treated as a minor operational change; no disclosure required since IPEV allows both
Treated as a material change, requiring compliance with SEBI disclosure and reporting guidelines and PPM update

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 14.14, 'any change in the valuation methodology or approach shall be construed as a MATERIAL CHANGE significantly influencing the decision of the investor'. The AIF must comply with SEBI disclosure/reporting guidelines and update the PPM with details of the change, accounting impact and valuation impact. **The Trap:** Option A is the 'IPEV permits any method' trap — IPEV flexibility does not override SEBI disclosure. Option C invents a 5% threshold. Option D confuses material change with prior-approval items. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A (Compliance) teaches material-change concept generically. XIX-C demands the AIF-specific treatment: PPM annual update + LP intimation + audit-trail on old-and-new methodology NAVs. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When switching methodology, run BOTH methods in parallel for one reporting quarter and disclose both NAVs. This 'bridge period' transparency is what sophisticated LPs expect and prevents surprise at the next LPAC.
